test: Compute price-to-list (sum unit_price*qty / sum list_price*qty) by year and product category, separating lines with and without markdown. Decompose the yearly change into rate vs mix using fixed 2016 weights (by sku, and by customer). Check whether line-weighted customer discount_pct rises because of customers onboarded later (cohort by onboarded_day) vs mix shift among existing accounts, and whether price/list net of discount_pct and markdown is stable (i.e. price = list*(1-discount)*(1-markdown)).
support: Price-to-list falls in parts, supplies and refrigeration (non-markdown categories) as well as equipment; the within-sku/within-customer rate effect explains a material part of the decline; later-onboarded customers carry higher discount_pct and take a growing share of lines.
weaken: Price-to-list is flat outside equipment and markdown lines, so the decline is H1 markdowns plus mix; or the discount rise is a small share of the margin decline (0.1415->0.1518 is ~1 point of the ~4 point price-to-list drop).
expect: Moderately confident (60%) the hypothesis mostly does NOT hold as stated: I expect non-equipment price-to-list to move by about 1 point driven by customer mix/new accounts, and most of the ~4-point decline to sit in equipment markdowns (H1). Discount creep likely real but small, perhaps $1-2M/yr of the $6.5M.
